subject: Food Science
title: Discovery of Calories
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Discovery of Calories.

hook.text: Wilbur Atwater built the first human calorimeter in 1896—a sealed room that measured every calorie a person burned by tracking.

buildup.text: Atwater determined the caloric values used today: protein = 4 cal/g, carbohydrate = 4 cal/g, fat = 9 cal/g, alcohol = 7 cal/g.

discovery.text: His 'Atwater factors' were derived by burning food in a bomb calorimeter then subtracting losses from digestion.

twist.text: Atwater factors are averages with 5–25% error for individual foods. A raw almond delivers 20% fewer calories than the label.

climax.text: The FDA requires calorie counts on all US food labels since 1990. Atwater's 1896 system remains the legal basis for every.

punchline.text: One man, one sealed room, 1896. His calorie measurements power every food label on Earth.
